claims.text: Eutectic Al0.7CoCrFeNi has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and exhibits brittle behavior.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal phase boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittle failure in the untreated alloy.
The proposed intervention is cryogenic pre-straining at 77 K to approximately 5–10% strain before room-temperature tensile testing.
Cryogenic pre-straining under controlled strain magnitude and rate will produce uniformly distributed deformation twins in the FCC lamellae.
The deformation twins will act as additional dislocation sinks.
The deformation twins will provide alternate slip systems.
Twin boundaries will absorb and redistribute dislocations during subsequent room-temperature deformation.
Dislocation absorption and redistribution by twin boundaries will reduce dislocation pile-ups at lamellar interfaces.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will mitigate local stress concentrations.
Mitigating local stress concentrations will delay microcrack initiation under tensile loading.
Cryogenically pre-strained material will have greater room-temperature tensile elongation than untreated material.
Cryogenically pre-strained material will maintain or slightly increase yield strength relative to untreated material.
The anticipated strength and ductility improvements result from more homogeneous plastic deformation and delayed crack initiation.
The untreated as-cast or conventionally processed alloy combines high yield strength with limited tensile ductility.
The predicted improvements apply under room-temperature tensile loading after cryogenic pre-straining and equilibration.
Departures from the intended pre-strain parameters or nonuniform twin formation may reduce the beneficial effects.
